story.title: Court Dismisses Impeachment Threat Against South Africa's Ramaphosa
story.summary: A South African court has ruled in favor of President Cyril Ramaphosa, dismissing a report that had fueled impeachment efforts against him. The report was related to a cash theft incident at his private farm, which occurred in 2020. This ruling provides Ramaphosa with a reprieve from the impeachment threat.

event_overview.title: About Farmgate Scandal
event_overview.subject: Farmgate Scandal
event_overview.summary: The Farmgate, or Phala Phala, scandal concerns a February 2020 burglary at President Cyril Ramaphosa’s private Phala Phala wildlife farm in Limpopo, where foreign currency was stolen, and the subsequent questions about the money, the reporting of the crime, and the use of state resources. It produced separate criminal, regulatory, ethics and parliamentary-impeachment processes, whose mandates and outcomes were not the same.

facts.label: Incident
facts.value: The underlying burglary occurred on or about 9 February 2020 at Phala Phala farm in the Waterberg area of Limpopo Province, and involved the theft of foreign currency.

facts.label: Criminal case
facts.value: In November 2026, the Modimolle Regional Court found two of three accused guilty in connection with the farm theft and acquitted the third; this criminal trial concerned the alleged perpetrators of the burglary rather than an adjudication of presidential impeachment allegations.

facts.label: Reserve Bank inquiry
facts.value: The South African Reserve Bank completed a foreign-exchange-control investigation on 14 August 2023. Its stated remit was limited to possible contraventions of the Exchange Control Regulations, and it said it could not conclude that Ramaphosa or Ntaba Nyoni Estates CC had contravened Regulation 6(1).

facts.label: Ethics inquiry
facts.value: The Public Protector’s 2023 report examined alleged breaches of the Executive Ethics Code by Ramaphosa and alleged improper conduct by police connected to the theft; it was an ethics and public-administration investigation, distinct from the theft prosecution and the Reserve Bank’s exchange-control review.

facts.label: Parliamentary accountability process
facts.value: The controversy also triggered a proposed removal process under section 89 of South Africa’s Constitution. On 25 November 2026, the Western Cape High Court reviewed and set aside the National Assembly independent panel’s report and steps taken pursuant to it.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the November 2026 theft verdict and the later court ruling on the impeachment-related panel report; it does not attempt to catalogue every investigation, allegation, hearing, appeal or political response in the broader Phala Phala matter.

related_stories.title: Israeli Judges Recommend Dropping Charges Against Netanyahu in Corruption Trial
related_stories.summary: Judges in Israel have recommended dropping one of the most serious charges in the corruption trial against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who faces accusations of bribery, fraud, and breach of trust. This recommendation has been seen as a significant boost for Netanyahu, who has consistently denied any wrongdoing. The trial, which began in 2020, has been a contentious issue in Israeli politics, particularly as Netanyahu seeks to maintain his political position.

related_stories.title: Russian Strikes Kill Seven in Ukraine; Kyiv Targets Refineries
related_stories.summary: Russian drone attacks resulted in the deaths of seven people across six Ukrainian regions, targeting infrastructure including a gas production facility and a thermal power plant. In response, Ukraine launched drone strikes on Russian oil refineries in the Samara and Rostov regions, as well as an airbase in Nizhny Novgorod, leading to at least one reported death in the Samara region.
